Subject: Quick follow-up: VPC/on-prem next steps & timeline

Hi Sabrina —

Great to meet today — thanks for walking us through FinLytics' privacy and throughput requirements. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on timing:   

- Recap:
  - Primary goal: move sensitive inference for user PII to a VPC/private deployment (initially in us-east).
  - Target load: ~120 QPS peak, typical 40 QPS sustained.
  - Key blockers: SOC2 evidence, legal redlines, procurement timeline.

- Suggested next steps: 
  1) We’ve attached a short VPC checklist and a mutual-action-plan (attached) with owners and ETA columns — would you review and flag a realistic procurement lead time?
  2) Security copy: we'll send SOC2 artifacts and architecture diagrams to your ops/legal contacts upon NDA.
  3) Pilot scope: 2-week private pilot (dedicated pool) to validate latency and KV cache behavior — can start as soon as legal signs MSA + SOW.

As for timeline, our typical ramp to a private pilot is ~4–8 weeks from signed SOW depending on procurement. I’ve included a preliminary cost band in the MAM (row: pilot estimate). If procurement needs an internal cost center estimate or a PO template, happy to provide that.

Action items for you: please confirm (A) procurement timeline (B) who on your side will handle legal redlines (C) whether ops wants the architecture doc now or after NDAs.

I've attached: redwood-vpc-checklist.pdf, mutual-action-plan.xlsx

If easier, I can do a 15-min call with your legal/ops next week to go through SOW highlights — what time zone works best?

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0172

Hi Sabrina — thanks for the quick note. Answers below and a couple of small clarifications.

- Ballpark run-rate: for a dedicated pool sized to meet ~120 QPS peak with burst headroom, expect $35k–$50k/mo (depends on acceptable latency SLO and whether you want strict isolation vs. shared-dedicated lanes). I put a worked example in the MAM under "pilot estimate" and included optional quantization savings.
- KMS: yes — we support customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS/HSM) in VPC/private deployments; we'll include the KMS integration notes in the architecture doc.

Clarifications: the pilot scope we recommended is scoped to validate latency and cache behavior — if you want to include an eval of long-tail prompts / larger context lengths, we should size the pool accordingly (possible +20–30% on cost).

I also dropped a link in HubSpot for the deal (https://hub.redwood.ai/deals/RDW-FTX-349) and uploaded a short architecture diagram to the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B_vpc-mam
